h1: Cana Boutique Hotel — a spotless family-run boutique in Thonburi, 14 minutes to Bangkok's Southern Bus Terminal
intro: Tucked into a quiet lane in Bang Phlat on Bangkok's Thonburi side, a small owner-run boutique hotel has been winning guests over with cleanliness that genuinely surprises and hospitality that feels personal — Cana Boutique Hotel is a 31-room, 3-star property about 500 m from MRT Bang Yi Khan (Blue Line) and a 14-minute Grab ride (6 km) from Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai) — there is no direct hotel shuttle, so you rely on Grab or a meter taxi, but the route is short and straightforward · pets welcome · from approx ฿1,200/night, breakfast included

body.html: Cana Boutique Hotel sits at 139 Soi Charan Sanitwong 57/2, Bang Bumru sub-district, Bang Phlat district — Thonburi's quieter western fringe, away from Sukhumvit-side crowds · the hotel is entirely family-run, and what guests mention most, returning trip after trip through the reviews, is a level of cleanliness that frequently draws comments like "the cleanest hotel I have stayed in Bangkok" and a welcome from the owners that extends to carrying bags upstairs, hand-drawing maps to the MRT, and troubleshooting late arrivals.

There are 31 rooms across three floors with no elevator — a genuine drawback if you are travelling with heavy luggage or elderly companions, so it is worth flagging honestly before you book · room categories run from Deluxe and Deluxe Triple through Family Queen and Family Classic up to Junior Suite · every room comes with a smart TV, mini-bar fridge, kettle, bathrobes, slippers and a complete bathroom set · the Family and Junior Suite options have enough space for three or four people and some include a microwave and dining area.
"Staff were first-rate, very helpful and welcoming. Breakfast was delicious — the menu to choose from was quite expansive. Rooms are so clean and nice."

The breakfast here punches above its weight for a property this size · multiple guests describe a spread of both Thai and Western dishes cooked fresh each morning — not the toast-and-a-sachet-of-coffee that small hotels often default to · breakfast is served 07:00–10:30 and is included in the room rate for all room types · the on-site restaurant and snack bar are also open for lunch and dinner if you prefer to stay in.

The location picture needs to be clear before you book · the hotel is not within walking distance of Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai) — the terminal sits on Borommaratchachonnani Road in Taling Chan, about 6 km away, and the journey by Grab or meter taxi takes roughly 14 minutes in normal traffic · MRT Bang Yi Khan is a genuinely easy 500-metre walk from the hotel, but the Blue Line does not serve Sai Tai Mai — for the bus terminal you will always need a car or taxi · the logic for bus travellers is to sleep here the night before an early departure, eat a proper breakfast, and then call a Grab: the ride is short, affordable and much more comfortable than loitering at the terminal overnight.

Drawing on the full spread of real guest reviews, a few honest points deserve mention · some room types have no natural windows, particularly on the lower floors, and at least one guest found their room did not match the booking description — specifying "window room" in the special-request field when booking is advisable · soundproofing between rooms is thin: light sleepers can pick up noise from neighbouring units · one reviewer raised a pest concern, though this sits in notable contrast to the overwhelming majority who praise the cleanliness · check-in closes at 21:00, which is earlier than most hotels in Bangkok — travellers arriving late must contact the hotel in advance or risk being locked out.

For travellers heading to Hua Hin, Krabi, Phuket, Kanchanaburi, Surat Thani or other southern and western destinations by long-distance coach, the overall proposition is sound · prices run from approximately ฿1,200–1,500 per night for a standard Deluxe room in the low-to-mid season, rising to ฿2,000–2,500 for Family rooms and ฿2,500–3,000 for the Junior Suite during high season (December–March) · free parking is available, a real bonus for anyone driving to the hotel and then travelling onward by bus · the hotel holds SHA (Safety and Health Administration) certification from the Tourism Authority of Thailand.

Additional facilities include free Wi-Fi throughout, laundry service, luggage storage, a 24-hour front desk, childcare assistance and airport transfers for a fee · dogs are accepted on request and with an additional fee — a rare find in this part of Thonburi, making Cana a practical choice for pet owners who want to break a road journey at a quiet west-side hotel before heading down south.

highlights.text: Dogs accepted on request (fee applies). Free private parking for cars. MRT Bang Yi Khan 500 m on foot — rare combination in Thonburi west.

honestSummary: Cana Boutique Hotel is at its best for travellers who need to catch an early or late long-distance coach from Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai) and want a genuinely clean, well-run boutique to sleep in the night before — the 14-minute Grab ride to the terminal is short and easy · free parking and pet-acceptance add practical value · the honest caveats: no elevator, some rooms have no windows, and check-in closes at 21:00.
honestChecks: If you are arriving in Bangkok after 21:00 — check-in closes at 21:00 and the hotel is strict about it · contact the property before booking to arrange a late arrival or you may find yourself turned away → always message them directly to confirm.

If you have heavy luggage or mobility issues — there is no elevator and the building has three floors · ask for a ground-floor room via the special-request field when booking, and confirm they can accommodate you.

If natural light in your room matters to you — some room types on lower floors have no windows · write 'window room please' in your booking notes and follow up with the hotel to make sure you get one.

tips.title: Book your Grab to Sai Tai Mai the night before
tips.body: No hotel shuttle exists — use the Grab app to schedule a car to Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai) the night before, especially for pre-dawn departures. The 6-km ride takes about 14 minutes and drivers are usually available in this area.

tips.title: Request a ground-floor room if you have heavy bags
tips.body: The building has no elevator. Three floors of stairs with a large suitcase is hard work. Put 'ground floor please' in the special-request field when booking — and confirm with the hotel directly.

tips.title: Ask for a room with windows
tips.body: Some lower-floor rooms have no natural light. If daylight matters to you, note 'window room required' in your booking comment and follow up via the hotel's messaging channel to confirm before arrival.

tips.title: Travelling with a dog? Call ahead
tips.body: Dogs are accepted subject to availability and an additional fee. Rare to find in Thonburi west. Contact the hotel directly before booking to confirm the policy, the fee, and whether space is available on your dates.

faq.q: How do I get from Cana Boutique Hotel to Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai)?
faq.a: There is no hotel shuttle. Call a Grab or meter taxi from in front of the hotel — the distance is approximately 6 km and the journey takes around 14 minutes in normal traffic along Borommaratchachonnani Road · MRT Bang Yi Khan is a short 500-metre walk from the hotel, but the Blue Line does not serve Sai Tai Mai, so a car or taxi is the only option for that route.

faq.q: Does Cana Boutique Hotel have an elevator?
faq.a: No elevator. The building has three floors and guests must use the stairs · if you have heavy luggage or reduced mobility, request a ground-floor room in the special-request field when booking, and confirm with the hotel before arrival.

faq.q: What time is check-in, and does the hotel accept pets?
faq.a: Check-in is 14:00–21:00 · if you are arriving after 21:00 you must contact the hotel in advance — they have been known to be strict on this and late arrivals without prior notice can be turned away · dogs are accepted on request with an additional fee; contact the hotel directly to confirm availability and the exact charge before booking.

faq.q: Is breakfast included at Cana Boutique Hotel?
faq.a: Yes — breakfast is included in the room rate for all room types, served 07:00–10:30 · reviews consistently praise the spread: a mix of freshly cooked Thai dishes and Western options that goes well beyond the usual toast-and-instant-coffee.

faq.q: What are the room prices at Cana Boutique Hotel?
faq.a: Prices start from approximately ฿1,200–1,500/night for a Deluxe room in the low-to-mid season · Family Queen rooms run around ฿2,000 · Junior Suites from ฿2,500 · high season (December–March) and Thai public holidays will push prices higher — book in advance and use free-cancellation rates wherever possible.

faq.q: What destinations can I reach from Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai)?
faq.a: Sai Tai Mai on Borommaratchachonnani Road in Taling Chan is Bangkok's main long-distance coach terminal for the west and south of Thailand · direct services include Hua Hin, Cha-am, Prachuap Khiri Khan, Chumphon, Surat Thani, Krabi, Phuket, Kanchanaburi, Nakhon Si Thammarat and many more · most operators run overnight coaches as well as daytime services.
